r0.why: Theory of large plates moving since 3-4 billion years ago [1], lithosphere as rigid shell with crust and upper mantle and seven or eight major plates [5], builds on continental drift [2], accepted after seafloor spreading validated in 1960s [3].

r1.why: Division into lithosphere and asthenosphere [21], cooler and more rigid versus hotter and flowing [23], rigid plates floating on ductile asthenosphere beneath [16], key principle [26].

r2.why: Plate boundary definition [42], relative motion sets convergent, divergent or transform [6], geological events and features [43], volcanoes and Ring of Fire [44].

r3.why: Subduction carrying a plate edge into the mantle [10], reducing surface area [11], balanced by new oceanic crust at divergent margins, conveyor belt [12].

r4.why: Lateral density variations and convection currents [17], ridge as topographic high with cooling crust adding to motion [18], sinking cold dense crust as strongest driver [19], other factors such as lunar tidal drag debated [20].

r5.why: Zero to 10 cm annually [7]; 10 to 40 mm at Mid-Atlantic Ridge like fingernails and about 160 mm for Nazca plate like hair [27].

r6.why: One or two crust types over lithospheric mantle [28], oceanic crust formed at spreading centers [30], denser with less silicon [32], below sea level versus buoyant continental crust [33].

r7.why: Earth only planet known with active plate tectonics, other bodies show tectonic activity [13], Europa's ice plates [14], Mars and Venus in the past but not same form [15].
